Array By ID Merge Behavior

Array By ID Merge is a Merge Behavior that combines array-based State values by an identifier property during the Merge Stage.

The Behavior updates an existing entity when its identifier matches the incoming entity and appends incoming entities with new identifiers. The identifier property is selected through the FluentApi configuration.

Array By ID Merge supports deletion of matching entities through the Merge configuration supplied with a merge-style State update. The Behavior returns the merged State value for the remaining Pipeline Stages.

Note

The Merge Stage is entered through explicit State-update APIs. A merge-style update supplies the incoming value and optional Merge configuration to the active Merge Behavior.

Diagrams
Configuration

Array By ID Merge is configured for a through the Merge Stage. The Behavior requires an identifier property name before the is initialized.

Exactly one Merge Behavior is active for a at any time. When Array By ID Merge is registered, it becomes the active Merge Behavior for that .

ArrayByIdMergeOptions
Property Description
idKey: string

required

 Property name used to identify matching entities.
Note

The isDelete option is supplied with an individual merge-style update. When enabled, incoming entity identifiers identify entities to remove from the current array.

Evaluation Outcomes

Array By ID Merge evaluates the current committed State and the incoming resolved value to produce one merged result during the Merge Stage.

When an incoming value is undefined, the clearUndefined Merge configuration determines whether the current State is preserved or cleared. This option applies to the merge-style update and does not change the identifier configuration.

Examples

Example 1: Configure Array By ID Merge in a FeatureCell

This example registers Array By ID Merge for an employee array and configures id as the identifier property. The uses the FluentApi before initialization. 

{{`// app.config.ts
export const appConfig: ApplicationConfig = {
  providers: [
    provideVault({ logLevel: 'off' }),

    provideFeatureCell(
      EmployeeService
      {
        key: 'employees',
        initialState: []
      },
      [
        // Explicitly attach the Array By ID merge behavior
        withArrayByIdMergeBehavior
      ]
    )
  ]
};`}}

{{`@FeatureCell`}}<Employee[]>{{`('employees')
@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class EmployeeService {
  readonly vault = injectVault`}}<Employee[]>{{`(EmployeeService);

  constructor() {
    this.vault
      .withArrayMergeId({ idKey: 'id' })
      .initialize();
  }
}`}}
 
{{`export const employeeCell = FeatureCell`}}<Employee[]>{{`(
  {
    key: 'employees',
    initialState: []
  },
  [withArrayByIdMergeBehavior]
);

employeeCell
  .withArrayMergeId({ idKey: 'id' })
  .initialize();`}}

Example 2: Update and Delete Entities by Identifier

The incoming entity with an existing identifier updates that entity. A merge-style update with isDelete removes matching entities from the current array. 

{{`this.vault.mergeState({
  value: { id: 1, name: 'Grace Hopper' }
});

this.vault.mergeState(
  { value: { id: 2 } },
  { isDelete: true }
);`}}
 
{{`employeeCell.mergeState({
  value: { id: 1, name: 'Grace Hopper' }
});

employeeCell.mergeState(
  { value: { id: 2 } },
  { isDelete: true }
);`}}

Example 3: Merge and Delete Arrays of Entities

An array merge can update one existing entity and append another in the same merge-style update. An array supplied with isDelete removes each matching entity by identifier. 

{{`this.vault.mergeState({
  value: [
    { id: 1, name: 'Grace Hopper' },
    { id: 3, name: 'Katherine Johnson' }
  ]
});

this.vault.mergeState(
  {
    value: [
      { id: 1 },
      { id: 2 }
    ]
  },
  { isDelete: true }
);`}}
 
{{`employeeCell.mergeState({
  value: [
    { id: 1, name: 'Grace Hopper' },
    { id: 3, name: 'Katherine Johnson' }
  ]
});

employeeCell.mergeState(
  {
    value: [
      { id: 1 },
      { id: 2 }
    ]
  },
  { isDelete: true }
);`}}
